content.title: Justin Rose majors timeline: Inside the golfer's last major win and more
content.text: Justin Rose majors timeline: Inside the golfer's last major win and more originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.Justin Rose turned professional 28 years ago, but he found himself facing off with much younger competition at Augusta National in 2025.AdvertisementThe English golfer cruised through the opening rounds of the Masters, but ultimately fell to Rory McIlroy in a playoff, as the latter completed the career Grand Slam.Rose found himself in nearly the same position as a top contender at the Open Championship in 2024. After entering the final round one shot off the lead and initially looking strong, he finished second behind Xander Schauffele.And Rose is contending at the Masters once again in 2026, and his familiar foe in McIlroy is also in contention. Here's what you need to know about Rose's history in majors.MORE:Has Justin Rose won a major?Rose has one major victory, coming at the 2013 U.S. Open, at Merion Golf Club near Philadelphia.AdvertisementIn a tournament that presented a remarkable challenge for the entire field — no one finished under par — consistency was the difference for Rose. He shot either a 69, 70 or 71 in each of his four rounds, finally overtaking Phil Mickelson for the lead late in the final round and holding on over the last five holes to win by two strokes.It was a monumental moment for Rose, who turned professional at just 19 and struggled early in his career. He had been building to the victory with six top-10 major finishes leading up to 2013, and the victory remains the pinnacle of Rose's career.MORE: Why is the Masters always at Augusta?How old is Justin Rose?Rose is 45. He's set to turn 46 on July 30.AdvertisementA Masters win would make Rose the second-oldest player to ever win a green jacket, behind Jack Nicklaus, who won at age 46 in 1986.MORE:Every Masters winner, by yearJustin Rose Masters historyRose hasn't won the Masters, but he's generally performed well at Augusta by making the cut in all but three of his appearances. He's made the cut in 16 of those appearances, with his best finishes coming in 2015, 2017 and 2025 when he ranked second on the final leaderboard.AdvertisementRose came painfully close to a win in 2017, as he missed a putt on the 18th hole and ultimately lost a playoff to Sergio Garcia after Garcia missed one as well.MORE TO KNOW ABOUT THE MASTERSJustin Rose majors resultsHere's a look at Rose's results in all of the majors throughout his career.YearMastersPGA ChampionshipU.S. OpenOpen Championship1998———T-41999———Cut2001———T-302002—T-23—T-222003T-39CutT-5Cut2004T-22CutCut—2005————2006—T-41——2007T-5T-12T-10T-122008T-36T-9CutT-702009T-20CutCutT-132010—Cut—Cut2011T-11CutCutT-442012T-8T-3T-21Cut2013T-25T-331Cut2014T-14T-24T-12T-232015T-24T-27T-62016T-10T-22CutT-2220172CutCutT-542018T-12T-19T-10T-22019CutT-29T-3T-202020T-239Cut—20217T-8CutT-462022CutT-13T-37—2023T-16T-9CutCut2024CutT-6CutT-220252CutCutT16
